newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM, M-Serla stakes in M-Botnia unchanged.
newsitem.headline: UPM, M-Serla stakes in M-Botnia unchanged.

text.p: Finnish forest industry groups UPM-Kymmene Oy and Metsa-Serla Oy said on Tuesday their ownership stakes in pulp mill Metsa-Botnia would remain unchanged at 47 percent and 52 percent respectively.

A series of deals between the two companies announced on Tuesday will include increasing the share capital of Metsa-Botnia, and raise loans, to make possible a 650 million markka investment in UPM's Joutseno pulp mill, which will be bought and upgraded by Metsa-Botnia.
"Metsa-Botnia's ownership, 52 percent held by Metsa-Serla, one percent by Metsaliitto and 47 percent by UPM-Kymmene will remain unchanged," Metsa-Serla said in a statement.
For UPM-Kymmene, the value of the sales of units to Metsa-Serla and Metsa-Botnia would be nearly two billion markka, it said in a separate statement, adding Metsa-Serla would pay nearly half in cash.

"The balance UPM-Kymmene will invest in Metsa-Botnia's shares and in a shareholder loan to be granted to the company so as to maintain the current ownership structure and to finance the investment in Joutseno Pulp," it said.
Metsa-Serla said it would pay UPM-Kymmene 870 million markka in cash. This would be financed from its recent sale for 1.05 billion markka of its chemicals operations.

"As a result of these arrangements, Metsa-Serla's equity to assets ratio will remain around 40 percent while the balance sheet will increase by 1.9 billion markka and annual turnover (rise) by 1.8 billion markka. Interest-bearing debts will grow by 1.4 billion markka," the company said.
In 1995, Metsa-Serla's balance sheet was 18.6 billion markka, turnover was 13.1 billion markka and total liabilities 10.9 billion markka. Its equity-assets ratio was 42.4 percent.
UPM-Kymmene said the combined net sales of the units to be sold in Simpele and Joutseno were two billion markka, of which UPM group internal sales accounted for 1.3 billion.
"Joutseno Pulp is UPM-Kymmene's only non-integrated chemical pulp mill," it said, adding this made it "better suited to be a part of Metsa-Botnia."
